note.summary: This chunk explains CGT rules for personal representatives and legatees administering a deceased person's estate: assets are rebased to market value at date of death, personal representatives get a full AEA for up to 3 tax years, and the CGT rate for personal representatives (and trustees) is 24% for disposals on or after 30 October 2024. It covers deductible administration expenses (including HMRC's SP02/04 scale), how assets transfer CGT-free to legatees at death value, valuation rules where IHT and CGT values must match ('ascertained' values), and conditions for deeds of variation to be read back into the will for CGT purposes under TCGA 1992 s.62(6).

4e44d8e4ca9aec44.heading: Capital Gains Tax when someone dies (Self Assessment helpsheet HS282)

caveats: This helpsheet is for the tax year 2025 to 2026.
Terms mostly refer to England and Wales law; Scotland/Northern Ireland terminology and general law background may differ.
AEA is not available if the deceased died before 6 April 2025, was non-domiciled in the UK, and claimed the remittance basis on foreign income and gains.
From 6 April 2025 the remittance basis of taxation is no longer available.
If the deceased died before 6 April 2025, their domicile status may also be relevant to residence status determination for personal representatives.
Losses in the year of death must be set off against gains even if net chargeable gains fall below the AEA; unused losses cannot be used by personal representatives or legatees.
No CGT charge arises on death itself; special deemed-transfer rules apply instead.

For CGT purposes, someone who benefits from a testamentary disposition (usually a will) or on intestacy/partial intestacy; includes trustees of a settlement made under the will or intestacy.

note.summary: HS282 explains how CGT applies when someone dies, covering the treatment of personal representatives, the administration period, legatees, and intestacy. It sets out that assets are deemed transferred at market value on the date of death, describes reporting and payment obligations for UK property disposals, and details AEA availability and loss carry-back rules with a worked example for 2025-26. It also covers residence/domicile status of the deceased and personal representatives, and pre-death CGT liability agreement.
